KEY MESSAGE 1...Low pressure developing well off the East Coast
will strengthen and move north towards the Mid Atlantic coast 
and southern New England this weekend. This will bring potential
for rain across the region and strong winds near the coast.

Strong high pressure remains in place across eastern Canada, 
and it will hold fast through today before slowly weakening. 
Meanwhile, low pressure is organizing and strengthening well 
offshore of the North Carolina coast and it will further deepen 
and track northward through Saturday. The exact track that this
low is still somewhat uncertain. Still, the strengthening 
pressure gradient between the approaching low and high to the
north will continue to result in persistent north to northeast 
winds across our region through Saturday, strongest along the
immediate coast. The Wind Advisory for the Atlantic coastal 
zones was extended in time through Friday, as sustained winds
will likely remain near 25-35 mph with gusts of 40-50 mph at 
times.

The main impacts of the approaching storm still look to be
primarily for Marine and Coastal-land areas, with tidal 
flooding and strong gusty winds along the coast and most of our
tidal water bodies and waterways. Inland winds will be gusty as
well (mostly 20-30 mph). Details regarding the surf and coastal
flooding can be found in the relevant Key Messages below.

The latest 00Z suite of guidance has generally shifted
westward again with the track of the low moving north, most 
concerning during the Friday night through Saturday time frame.
There is still a considerable amount of spread in the track 
guidance, especially for being only roughly 48 hours out from 
the storm approaching the coast. Examination of the modeled 
upper level wind fields and jet dynamics suggest an "out to sea"
track is highly unlikely. The question is how close will the 
low get to our coastline locally, and how strong will it be when
it gets there. The latest trends suggest it could certainly get
close enough Friday night and/or Saturday during its peak 
strength to cause high winds along our immediate coastline 
(storm force wind gusts over the ocean waters). The exact track 
and strength will also dictate the exact wind direction, and 
thus whether winds will be more offshore (best case scenario), 
shore parallel, or onshore (worst case scenario). These details 
remain unclear, and guidance will be monitored closely to assess
and fine tune details regarding relevant impacts to our coastal
areas.

Due to the potential for high winds along the immediate coast, 
a High Wind Watch was issued, which is in effect 6 PM Friday 
through 6 PM Saturday. Sustained winds of 30-40 mph with gusts 
up to 60 mph are not out of the realm of possibility within the 
watch area. If the storm tracks very close to the coast, wind 
gusts of 40-50 mph could potentially reach inland across the 
coastal plain southeast of I-95, but again, this would be a 
worst case scenario.

The further west trend has resulted in an increase of the
probability of rain over the weekend, and PoPs have increased
across the board accordingly. However, excessive rainfall and
fresh water flooding related issues still appear unlikely at
this time. Rainfall amounts range from 0.10" in the far western
areas to around 1-1.50" along the northern New Jersey coast over
the course of 48+ hours.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Multiple rounds of significant tidal flooding 
expected into this weekend. Coastal Flood Warnings and 
Advisories remain in effect.

With a slow moving coastal storm and multiple days of strong 
northeast winds expected, the confidence in the threat for tidal
flooding remains high. Strong onshore flow that is projected to
last for several days will result in water piling up across 
tidal tributaries and within back bays of coastal communities. 
Tidal levels will also be enhanced with astronomical tides 
increasing with the upcoming Full Moon on Saturday. This 
combination of factors will lead to widespread tidal flooding, 
some of which will get well into Moderate stage. While not 
currently forecast, the threat for Major flooding is not off the
table, especially getting near the full moon. Tidal guidance 
diverges greatly beyond Thursday Night at nearly all of our 
forecast points. Some guidance has moderate to even major 
flooding for the weekend while some barely has tide levels 
getting into minor flood stage. It all will depend on the track 
of the coastal storm. 

No significant changes were made to the Coastal Flood Warnings 
and Advisories that are in effect through Friday evening. 
However, Warnings and/or Advisories may have to be extended into
Saturday depending on the exact track and strength of the low.
